t: In front of you is Morden College, a Grade I listed building in Blackheath. It has been providing residential care for over three hundred years. Sir John Morden, a successful merchant who briefly served as an MP, founded it in 1695 as a home for poor merchants, and it carries his name. The design is sometimes attributed to Sir Christopher Wren. Today it functions as a retirement home. Thomas Cooke, a Governor of the Bank of England, is buried here, and the businessman and politician Henry Newton Knights died here. In 2023, its day centre won the Stirling Prize for architecture.
